findings.title: Harvests on the To date are excluded from stats (range is end-exclusive)
findings.steps: Sample data has a Lettuce harvest of 150 g on 2026-09-30. Open /stats?from=2026-09-01&to=2026-09-30 (or call the API with from=2026-09-30&to=2026-09-30).
findings.expected: The 150 g Lettuce harvest is counted, because the To date is part of the range the user picked.
findings.actual: The page says '0 harvests from 1 Sept 2026 to 30 Sept 2026' and 'No harvests in this range'. A single-day range always comes back empty. The SQL in backend/routers/stats.py uses `harvested_on < ?` with date_to, so the To day is left out of the table, the totals and top_plants. In the default range this also drops harvests made on 31 Dec.
findings.evidence: The API returned months:[], plants:[], harvest_count:0 for from=to=2026-09-30. With from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-20 it returned only the 450 g Tomato harvest and left out the Courgette 1200 g harvest dated 2026-07-20. The page text showed the empty state.

findings.title: Dashboard top plant leaves out 31 Dec harvests, unlike the dashboard's own yearly totals
findings.steps: Log a large harvest dated 31 Dec of the current year for a plant that is not the current leader, then open the dashboard.
findings.expected: Top plant and its grams cover the whole year, the same as harvest_grams_year (which uses BETWEEN).
findings.actual: top_plant now comes from top_plants(), which uses `< year_end` (31 Dec). Harvests on 31 Dec count toward the year's harvest total but not toward the top plant, so the two numbers can disagree. The old code used BETWEEN, so this is a regression.
findings.evidence: dashboard.py: harvest totals use `BETWEEN ? AND ?`, while top_plants in stats.py uses `>= ? AND < ?` with date(year,12,31).

findings.title: Stats error state has no way to retry
findings.steps: Make GET /api/stats/harvests return 500 (mocked with a text/plain body), then click 'Stats' in the nav.
findings.expected: An error message with a Retry button that fetches again without reloading the page.
findings.actual: Only the alert 'Could not load harvest stats.' appears. There is no retry button, so the only way to retry is to change a date or reload the page.
findings.evidence: Snapshot of the main area: form, an empty paragraph, and alert 'Could not load harvest stats.'. No button.

findings.title: Stats request has no timeout, so a hung API leaves 'Loading stats…' on screen forever
findings.steps: Make /api/stats/harvests hang (never respond), then open /stats or change a date.
findings.expected: The request fails after 10 s and the page shows an error with a retry option.
findings.actual: useApiFetch/useApiClient set no `timeout`, so the request waits indefinitely and the page keeps showing 'Loading stats…'.
findings.evidence: No timeout option in composables/useApi.ts or in stats.vue.

findings.title: Clearing a date field silently uses a different range than the field shows
findings.steps: Clear the From field (or the To field).
findings.expected: Either refuse the empty value with a visible reason, or show the range actually used in the field.
findings.actual: The empty value is left out of the query, and the server quietly uses 1 Jan (or 31 Dec) of the current year. The field stays blank while the results are for a range the user never chose. Setting To to an earlier year with From cleared leads to a 422 error that is hard to understand.
findings.evidence: In stats.vue, the `query` computed leaves out empty values, and stats.py falls back to year_bounds(today).
